text: For smallholder pig farmers in Preah Vihear, pig housing should protect against heat, heavy rain, flooding, injury, predators, and disease while providing clean water, feeding space, drainage, and manure management. During the wet season (roughly May–October), good drainage is especially important since muddy pens and standing water increase hygiene and disease problems. During the dry season (roughly November–April), heat stress is a major concern since pigs have limited ability to sweat — shade, airflow, abundant clean water, and practical cooling matter. Biosecurity is particularly important for preventing African swine fever (ASF), classical swine fever, and other infectious diseases: avoid unnecessary mixing of pigs from different sources, obtain new pigs from known-health-status sources where possible, keep new pigs separate and monitored before joining the group, and never feed pigs untreated food waste containing pork or other animal products, since this is a serious ASF transmission pathway. Cleaning and disinfection should be routine, not only after disease appears; do not recommend a particular disinfectant concentration as a universal Cambodian dose — follow the product label or veterinary guidance. If pigs show rapidly spreading illness, sudden unexplained deaths, high fever, severe weakness, or hemorrhagic signs, stop unnecessary pig movement, separate affected animals where practical, and seek veterinary/animal-health assistance promptly — do not advise slaughtering, selling, or transporting apparently healthy pigs simply because some animals are sick. No specific pig breed is claimed as predominant in Preah Vihear without reliable evidence.
